findings.description: Enforcement-location mismatch + silent-overwrite gap on the actual read-back path. SHEET-MAP-002's text ('key mark read-back by row identity (symbol), asserting one row per symbol and erroring loudly if violated') reads, taken at face value, as a requirement on the mark READ-BACK process itself. All three A-sketches (A1/A2/A3) unanimously modeled it that way: a dedicated keying function that ingests already-read-back mark/price rows (MarkRow{symbol, price}) and returns Result<..., DuplicateError> on any repeat symbol. The real code does not enforce the invariant there at all. The actual mark read-back function, `read_marks` (lib.rs ~817-887), takes `symbols: &[Symbol]` and performs ZERO uniqueness checking on it -- its loop does `latest.insert(s.clone(), r.clone())` inside `for s in symbols`, a plain BTreeMap upsert: if `symbols` ever contained a duplicate, the second occurrence would silently overwrite the first (last-write-wins) -- the literal opposite of 'erroring loudly.' The actual `Err(ViewError::DuplicateSymbolRow(..))` guard lives one step upstream, in `render_positions` (lib.rs ~540-545), checking `snapshot.positions` (a `Map<Symbol,_>`) via a `BTreeSet<&Symbol>` seen-set -- and the code's own comments plus the test `duplicate_symbol_guard_is_defensive_and_one_row_per_symbol_holds` state explicitly that this guard is DEFENSIVE and 'structurally unreachable through the real API' because Map-backed `Snapshot.positions` already guarantees uniqueness. So the one place literally named 'read-back' has no assertion and would silently overwrite on a real violation, while the assertion that does exist sits earlier, over different data, and is dead code on the only real call path. All three B-reconstructions independently surfaced this exact fact from the code (B1: 'read_marks performs NO independent duplicate-detection... relies on render_positions's guard'; B2's 'Downstream keying' section; B3's U3) -- the same gap both directions converge on, just approached from opposite ends.

The error's Display format is a pinned code-side constant the spec text never states. `ViewError::DuplicateSymbolRow`'s Display impl is a literal Debug passthrough (`write!(f, "{self:?}")`), and the test `duplicate_symbol_guard_is_defensive_and_one_row_per_symbol_holds` pins the exact output string `DuplicateSymbolRow("AMZN")` -- no human-readable message at all. SHEET-MAP-002 says only 'erroring loudly,' nothing about message shape. All three B-runs independently called this out as a specific, test-pinned requirement. By contrast all three A-sketches invented descriptive, human-readable error text instead (A1/A3's thiserror derive messages like 'row identity violated: symbol ... appears at rows ... and ...'; A2's hand-rolled paragraph Display) -- since that A-side choice has no spec-text basis either, it's not itself an A-finding (unanimous invention, no basis), but it throws into relief that the code's actual minimalist Debug-passthrough convention is real, testable surplus the spec is silent on.

No normalization at the keying point -- exact-match only -- is a real, code-pinned fact absent from the spec text. All three B-runs state that symbol comparison for both row-identity keying and duplicate-detection is exact string/byte equality with no case-folding, trimming, or alias substitution (ticker aliasing via `resolve_ticker` is applied only to the displayed/formula ticker, never to the keying value) -- confirmed by the real code, where `render_positions`'s `BTreeSet<&Symbol>` check operates directly on the Symbol from `snapshot.positions` with no `.trim()`/case adjustment anywhere. SHEET-MAP-002 says nothing about normalization. Two of three A-sketches (A1, A3) invented a `.trim()` call before comparing (A2 did not) -- a minor unforced assumption with no spec basis and no code counterpart, consistent with the instructions' guidance that unanimous-or-near-unanimous inventions absent spec grounding are assumption artifacts, not findings -- flagged here since the B-side unanimously and correctly documents the real (stricter, non-normalizing) behavior as pinned surplus.

notes: Files reviewed: {scratch}/audit-baseline/crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs and .../tests/mapping.rs. A-direction: all 3 runs unanimously (a) build a standalone, exported keying function distinct from tab rendering, (b) return a Result-typed error (never panic), (c) treat empty-row-count as out of scope, (d) treat this as a per-invocation/stateless check, (e) do not attempt join-completeness against the ledger's expected symbol set. Splits are minor: trim-before-compare (A1, A3) vs no-trim (A2); EmptySymbol as a distinct error variant (A1, A3) vs absent (A2) -- neither split traces to spec text, so neither rises to a finding per the assumption-artifact rule. B-direction: all 3 runs converge almost verbatim on: one row per symbol in Positions via render_positions; the guard is a BTreeSet-based check returning Err(ViewError::DuplicateSymbolRow(Symbol)); the guard is defensive/structurally-unreachable given Snapshot.positions: Map<Symbol,_>; read_marks performs no independent dedup and trusts the caller; no normalization; Display=Debug passthrough pinned to the literal AMZN test string. No B-run materially disagrees with another. Given the primary finding is a genuine BD convergence (A models the check as living in the read-back function; B explicitly documents that the real read-back function has none and the real guard is dead/defensive code elsewhere), overall classification is BD-DRIFT even though two secondary B-only findings ride alongside it.
